division: Free State - Mangaung Metropolitan Municipality
name: OADC Bloemfontein (BFN1)
developer: Open Access Data Centres (OADC) / WIOCC Group
notes: OADC's Bloemfontein facility (BFN1) at 24 Barnes St, Bloemfontein (Mangaung Metro, Free State) provides colocation and metro connectivity to key data centres in the Bloemfontein area as part of OADC's pan-African network and South African edge data centre footprint; located adjacent to major fibre routes. No public MW capacity figure found; small regional/edge facility.

division: Free State - Thabo Mofutsanyana District Municipality
Free State - Xhariep District Municipality
Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Vantage JNB1 hyperscale campus (Waterfall City, Midrand)
notes: 80MW hyperscale campus in Waterfall City, Midrand (City of Johannesburg). First facility (JNB11) delivered/opened July 2022; phases 2 and 3 under construction per DC Pulse (2026). Part of Vantage's ~$1bn Africa entry; JNB1 is ~17km from Vantage JNB2 at Isando.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Africa Data Centres JHB1 (Midrand Campus)
notes: ADC's JHB1 campus in Midrand (City of Johannesburg) has ~8,500 sq m white space with up to 20MW IT load capacity (two 10MW facilities; latest hyperscale data centre completed 2021). 2N UPS topology with ~10 minutes battery autonomy at full load. ADC is Cassava Technologies' data centre arm.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Google Cloud Johannesburg region (first African cloud region)
notes: Google's first African cloud region, announced October 2022 and launched in Johannesburg in early 2024 (first GCP region launch of 2024), serving the Johannesburg area (City of Johannesburg). Part of Google's $1bn Africa investment. No public MW capacity.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Microsoft Azure South Africa North region (Johannesburg)
notes: Azure 'South Africa North' region in Johannesburg (datacenters.com lists a facility at 3012 William Nicol Drive, Bryanston, Sandton, City of Johannesburg). Region live since 2019; three Availability Zones now generally available. No public MW capacity.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Oracle Cloud Johannesburg region
notes: Oracle's first African cloud region went live 19 January 2022 (37th region globally), hosted in the Johannesburg area (City of Johannesburg). Oracle Interconnect for Microsoft Azure is available in Johannesburg for multi-cloud connectivity. No public MW capacity.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Huawei Cloud South Africa region (Johannesburg)
notes: Huawei Cloud unveiled its South African region in November 2018 and began local services in 2019, based in Johannesburg (City of Johannesburg); opened a Cloud & AI Innovation Centre in July 2020. MyBroadband reporting notes the region has struggled relative to AWS/Azure/Google. No public MW capacity.

division: Gauteng - City of Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality
name: Vodacom Midrand Data Park (Vodacom Business)
notes: Vodacom Business data centre at 82 Vodacom Boulevard, Midrand (City of Johannesburg); Vodacom operates an NB-IoT lab on the roof of its Midrand data centre (TechCentral). Directory-listed (Data Center Map) as Vodacom Johannesburg Data Center; no public MW capacity. Midrand is a major SA data centre hub.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: NTT Global Data Centers Johannesburg 1 (JOH1, Samrand)
notes: NTT's first African data centre, JOH1 at Centralpoint Innovation District, 21 Sterling Road, Samrand Business Park, Centurion - TechCentral notes it 'technically is in the City of Tshwane'. Tier III facility, two phases of 6MW each = 12MW total / ~6,000 sq m IT space; phase 1 completed 2021, full launch April 2022. Load-shedding immune design.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: Africa Data Centres Samrand Campus (expansion 10MW to 40MW)
notes: ADC's Samrand facility (built by Standard Bank in 2010 for R1.6bn as its primary data facility) at Samrand Business Park, Centurion (City of Tshwane; sources sometimes label it Johannesburg). ADC broke ground in Aug 2022 to expand from 10MW to 40MW IT load; widely regarded as one of Africa's top-specification data centres.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: Digital Parks Africa Samrand campus (expansion to 22MVA)
notes: Wholesale colocation operator Digital Parks Africa (DPA) is investing ~R500m (US$33.7m) to grow its Samrand campus in Centurion (City of Tshwane) to 22MVA capacity. Campus hosts carriers including WIOCC, SEACOM and Laser Light Africa. Existing facility operational; expansion announced 2023-24. Capacity in MVA, not MW.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: Hetzner JNB1 (Samrand Business Park)
notes: Hetzner JNB1 data centre at 21 Landmarks Avenue, Samrand Business Park, Centurion (City of Tshwane), per Inflect building listing (1 data center, 81 peers). Hetzner runs hosting data centre facilities in the Johannesburg/Tshwane area. No public MW capacity; directory-grade evidence.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: BCX / Telkom Centurion data centre
notes: Business Connexion (BCX), Telkom's IT services unit headquartered in Centurion (1021 Lenchen Avenue North, City of Tshwane), operates a data centre in Centurion; Telkom's Centurion data centre suffered a publicised network-switch outage in May 2017, confirming its operation. BCX also manages ~52 client data centres. No public MW capacity.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: Cavaleros Group proposed 200MW data centre near Pretoria
notes: Daily Maverick (Mar 2026) reported the Cavaleros Group was planning a 200MW data centre near Pretoria (City of Tshwane) and a 360MW campus in Cape Town, with the Pretoria plan announced in late 2025. Early-stage/planned; no dedicated press release or official confirmation found. Capacity per trade reporting.

division: Gauteng - City of Tshwane Metropolitan Municipality
name: Tshwane Data Centres (3 facilities, solar upgrade)
notes: Local operator 'Tshwane Data Centres' runs three data centre facilities in the City of Tshwane area; in 2023 it installed ~312kWp of solar (panels, inverters, batteries) with Red Energy across the three sites, plus a further 250kW SigenStor upgrade. Small local facilities; no public MW capacity figures.

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: Teraco Isando Campus (JB1/JB3/JB5)
notes: Teraco's Isando Campus (Isando, Kempton Park, Ekurhuleni - east of Johannesburg) comprises JB1 (~10MW), JB3 (30MW) and JB5 (30MW, completed 2024) = ~70MW critical power load; Africa's most interconnected facility with 14,000-16,500 interconnects. JB7 (40MW) construction adds to this campus (see separate line).

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: Teraco JB7 (Isando Campus expansion)
notes: 40MW hyperscale data centre at Teraco's Isando Campus, Ekurhuleni; construction began Nov 2024, scheduled for completion in 2026; 71,000 sq m facility funded by an R8bn (~$442m) syndicated loan; will take Isando Campus capacity to ~110MW. Built in a single phase with eight 1,500 sq m data halls.

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: Teraco Bredell Campus (JB2/JB4)
notes: Teraco's Bredell Campus in Bredell, Kempton Park (Ekurhuleni) comprises JB2 (opened 2017) and JB4 (38MW when announced, later expanded to ~50MW); campus totals ~64MW critical power load per Teraco platform data. JB4 has been billed as Africa's largest single data centre.

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: Equinix JN1 (Johannesburg IBX)
notes: Equinix's first South African IBX, JN1, at 233 Barbara Road, Elandsfontein, Germiston (Ekurhuleni); announced Dec 2022, came into service July 2024 and officially opened 23 Oct 2024. First phase 4MW power capacity, ~690 cabinets, 20,000 sq ft; hosts a JINX (Johannesburg Internet Exchange) node.

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: Vantage JNB2 hyperscale campus (Isando)
notes: Vantage's second Johannesburg campus, JNB2, at Brollo Road, Isando, Germiston - explicitly located in the City of Ekurhuleni, ~17km from JNB1 (Midrand). Construction announced Dec 2022; first building 20MW critical IT load / 33,000 sq m (355,000 sq ft) two-storey facility; DC Pulse lists launch for 2026.

division: Gauteng - Ekurhuleni Metropolitan Municipality
name: OADC Isando (JNB1) data centre
developer: Open Access Data Centres (OADC) / WIOCC Group
notes: OADC's Isando facility (JNB1) at 26 Electron Ave, Isando (Ekurhuleni) - carrier-neutral hyperscale core facility, ~7MW site load across 1,600+ sq m per OADC datasheet (OCOLO lists 12MW); phase 1 went >90% full within a year and phase 2 launched (~Q1 2024); Uptime Institute Tier-III design certified.

division: Gauteng - Sedibeng District Municipality
Gauteng - West Rand District Municipality
KwaZulu-Natal - Amajuba District Municipality
KwaZulu-Natal - eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality
name: Teraco Durban DB1 (Riverhorse Valley)
notes: Teraco's Durban data centre DB1 in Riverhorse Valley, north of Durban (eThekwini); expansion completed 2023 doubled capacity to 2.2MW critical power load (4MVA utility supply, 5,800 sq m, 700+ racks). Vendor-neutral colocation serving the KZN market.

division: KwaZulu-Natal - eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality
name: OADC Durban (Amanzimtoti)
developer: Open Access Data Centres (OADC) / WIOCC Group
notes: OADC Durban at Arbour Junction 2, Arbour Road, Amanzimtoti (eThekwini) went live April 2022 with 4MW power capacity; hosts the Durban landing of the 2Africa submarine cable (landed by WIOCC) and a 330kW on-site solar installation. 4,200 sq m facility with ~2,000 sq m IT white space.

division: KwaZulu-Natal - eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality
name: Dube TradePort data centre (La Mercy)
notes: Dube TradePort Corporation operates a data centre at its SEZ precinct in La Mercy, near King Shaka International Airport (eThekwini); a SABEN (SA NREN) RFP sought a link between the Teraco Durban datacentre and the Dube TradePort datacentre, confirming its existence. No public MW capacity; likely a modest facility.

division: KwaZulu-Natal - eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality
name: eThekwini AI data centre (Lovu River / Amanzimtoti, Korean consortium)
developer: eThekwini Municipality + Korea Southern Power (KOSPO) consortium
notes: eThekwini council (Feb/Mar 2026) approved a memorandum of agreement with a South Korean power consortium (Korea Southern Power Co./KOSPO reportedly involved) to explore a US$3-10bn AI data centre on a 5ha site at the mouth of the Lovu River near the Amanzimtoti Cable Landing Station (2Africa). Council briefing documents reference ~400MW (would be SA's largest, ~25% of Durban's electricity); eThekwini says MW figures are unconfirmed and the MOA is exploratory; target operational FY2027/28.
